headline: Broad-based growth as RTX raises full-year guidance again
summary_short: RTX's Q2 2026 sales rose 14.5% y/y to $24.71 billion with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.57 (adjusted EPS $1.89, +21% y/y), as operating margin expanded across all three segments and free cash flow reached $2.9 billion versus negative free cash flow a year ago.
summary_long: Sales grew 14% reported and 16% organically, with double-digit gains at all three segments — Collins Aerospace +8% on commercial OE/aftermarket growth, Pratt & Whitney +16% on aftermarket and F135 military volume, and Raytheon +18% on Patriot, Standard Missile, and AMRAAM demand. Adjusted operating margin expanded across all three segments, and adjusted EPS of $1.89 was up 21% y/y on higher segment operating profit. Operating cash flow was $3.5 billion and free cash flow $2.9 billion, versus negative free cash flow a year ago. Cash rose to $8.3 billion. RTX raised full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted sales, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow, citing backlog up 22% y/y to $289 billion.

drivers.explanation: CEO Chris Calio said RTX delivered "very strong second quarter results" with double-digit commercial aftermarket and defense growth, margin expansion across all three segments, and $2.9 billion of free cash flow, citing backlog up 22% y/y.

Growth was broad-based across all three segments: Collins Aerospace +8% (commercial OE, aftermarket, defense), Pratt & Whitney +16% (aftermarket, F135 military volume), and Raytheon +18% (Patriot, Standard Missile, AMRAAM demand).
Not a standalone line in the release; derived as net sales less cost of sales, both of which moved on the same segment-level volume drivers cited for revenue.
Segment operating profit grew on volume drop-through at Collins and Pratt & Whitney and favorable mix at Raytheon, partially offset by higher SG&A and prior-year divestiture effects at Collins.
Tracks operating profit growth (+31% y/y) plus lower net interest expense ($417M vs $457M a year ago); non-service pension income was roughly flat y/y.

Adjusted net income grew 22% y/y driven by adjusted segment operating profit growth across all three segments, per the release; GAAP net income also reflects a higher effective tax rate (18.0% vs 15.4%).
GAAP diluted EPS of $1.57 included $0.27 of acquisition accounting adjustments and $0.05 of restructuring/other items; adjusted diluted EPS of $1.89 was up 21% y/y on higher adjusted net income.
Tracks the same GAAP net-income growth as diluted EPS, divided by a weighted-average basic share count roughly flat y/y (1,350.7M vs 1,340.6M).
Balance-sheet short-term borrowings fell versus a year ago when the company had raised $1,432 million of commercial paper per the cash-flow statement; no comparable issuance occurred in Q2 2026.
Share count rose slightly y/y as RTX made no common-stock repurchases in Q2 2026 or Q2 2025 per the cash-flow statement, while stock compensation and 401(k) equity matching added shares.
